threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, target audience, and success criteria.

messages.text: Kicking off the Frontline Wellbeing & Communication Skills Program for contact centre and reception colleagues under project_pack_ref: Frontline Wellbeing & Communication Skills Program. The aim is to reduce stress and improve service quality through focused training and simple wellbeing routines. To get started, we need to align on pilot scope, target audience, and how we will know if the pilot works. I will start a light needs analysis for T1 and capture findings in A1 so we are not designing in the dark. @605 and @4784, can you help define which teams we include and rough headcount for T2 so we can draft A2 with a clear scope?

Thanks for starting this. For T2, my first thought is to include both the main contact centre floor and the ground-floor reception so we meet the requirement of at least two frontline teams. @45680 and @4784, could you share current headcount and shift patterns so we can see what is realistic without disrupting service? Once we have that, I can start drafting the pilot scope section in A2 and a first list of participants.

From the contact centre side, we have 24 agents across three main shift blocks. For a first pass, I suggest we focus on one pod per shift, so around 12 people total from the centre. That keeps us above minimum staffing while still giving us a decent sample. I can help you map this into T2 and later into the schedule for T6. For A1, I can also pull a quick list of the most common stressors we see in coaching notes and complaint escalations.

On reception we have 6 staff rotating across early and late shifts. Maybe we just include all 6 so we do not create confusion about who is in or out. I am not fully sure how many we can release at once without leaving the desk uncovered, but we can sort that out when we get to T6. For now, does 12 from the centre plus 6 from reception sound like a reasonable starting point for the pilot scope in A2?

On T1, I will run short interviews and a simple survey with at least 10 frontline colleagues and 3 supervisors. I will log stressors and skill gaps in A1. Initial themes I expect to test are: handling aggressive callers, managing back-to-back calls with no pause, and dealing with conflicting instructions from different departments. Once A1 has a first draft, we can check if the 18-person pilot group you are suggesting covers a mix of these situations.

So far we have: 12 contact centre agents (one pod per shift) and 6 reception staff, total 18 people. Unless there are strong objections, I will treat this as the working pilot scope for T2 and reflect it in A2. Selection criteria I am thinking of: mix of tenure (new and experienced), mix of call types or desk duties, and at least some volunteers who are keen to try wellbeing activities. @56723, can you confirm HR is comfortable with that approach before we lock it in?

From an HR point of view, that mix sounds fine as long as supervisors are involved in the final list and we avoid any perception of favouritism. We should also make sure we include a few part-time staff so we see how the program works with shorter shifts. If you add that note into T2 and A2, I am happy to support this as our proposed pilot group.

I can identify two part-time agents per shift who fit the criteria and are usually open to new initiatives. I will share names with you and @605 offline so you can complete T2. For reception, @4784, could you do the same and flag any constraints, like people who cannot be away from the desk for more than short periods?

Yes, I will draft a list for reception and note who can attend slightly longer sessions versus only shorter ones. I will send that to you and @605 so we can finalise the 6 names for T2. For the success side, I am wondering what we want to measure beyond attendance. Maybe fewer escalations and better mood scores in quick check-ins?

On success metrics, we need 2 or 3 that are simple to track. My suggestion: 1) a short self-reported stress rating before and after the pilot, captured in the survey for T9 and summarised later in A6; 2) a basic count of customer escalations or complaints from the pilot group compared to the previous period; 3) a quick confidence rating on handling difficult interactions. These can all be done with minimal extra admin.

I like those. For escalations, I can pull a simple baseline from our call logs for the 4 weeks before the pilot and then track the same group during the pilot window. For confidence, we can add one or two questions to the pre and post forms you are planning for T9. That way A6 will show both numbers and comments that we can use to refine the modules.

To summarise what I am hearing on metrics: 1) self-reported stress levels pre and post; 2) number of escalations or complaints involving the pilot group; 3) self-reported confidence in handling difficult calls or face-to-face situations. Unless anyone disagrees, I will document these as the primary success criteria in A2 so we have a clear reference when we evaluate the pilot.

No objections from me. Those three indicators feel concrete enough and still manageable. On the pilot group, I have checked the reception rota and can confirm that all 6 reception staff can be included as long as we stagger their sessions. So the 12 plus 6 proposal looks workable from my side.

Same here. I have reviewed the contact centre rosters and can confirm we can release 12 agents across the shifts without dropping below minimum staffing, as long as we design T6 carefully. I suggest we now formally confirm that the pilot will cover 12 contact centre agents and 6 reception staff so @605 can close T2 and update A2.

Agreed. From HR, I am comfortable confirming that the pilot scope is 18 participants: 12 from the contact centre and 6 from reception, selected using the criteria we discussed and validated with supervisors. Let us treat that as our confirmed pilot group and move ahead with T1 and T2 based on this.

I will update A2 today with the confirmed pilot group (12 contact centre agents and 6 reception staff) and the three success metrics we agreed. Once that is done, I will share the link in the channel so everyone can check for any gaps before we move on to detailed module design and scheduling.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalise the training modules and wellbeing protocol.

messages.text: Sharing a first draft of training topics and micro-break ideas for feedback. For the communication side under T3 and T7, I am proposing three modules for A3: 1) Handling angry or distressed callers/visitors; 2) Setting boundaries and using clear, calm language; 3) Recovering after a tough interaction and supporting colleagues. For wellbeing, @89425 has sketched some desk-based micro-breaks that would later be formalised in A4. Please review and comment before we lock anything in.

On the wellbeing side for T4, I am suggesting a set of 6 to 8 low-impact exercises suitable for desks: seated posture resets, neck and shoulder mobility, wrist and forearm relief, short standing stretch sequences, and a simple breathing pattern for quick reset. All of these can be done in normal work clothes and in small spaces. Once we agree on the list, I will document them clearly in A4 with step-by-step instructions and safety notes.

From the early interviews for T1 and notes in A1, the main stressors people mention are: frequent exposure to upset customers, feeling rushed with no time to reset, and uncertainty about what they are allowed to say. Your three proposed modules line up well with that. I would just emphasise that examples in A3 should use real phrases from our environment so people recognise their daily reality.

I like the three-module structure. For T7, I can help turn them into a simple slide deck and one-page job aid that fits into A3. One question: do we want a separate short segment on internal communication, for example how reception and the contact centre hand off tricky cases to each other, or do we weave that into the scenarios you are drafting for T3?

Maybe we can keep the three main modules as you proposed and include one or two handoff scenarios inside them. For example, a role-play where reception needs to transfer a distressed visitor to the contact centre or vice versa. That way we do not overload the agenda but still cover the cross-team angle. I can help draft those role-plays for T3 based on real calls and front-desk situations.

Good idea. For T3, I will outline 2 to 3 scenarios per module, including at least one that involves a handoff between reception and the contact centre. I will keep the structure consistent so T7 is easier to build: context, customer behaviour, staff response options, and debrief questions. Once I have a draft, I will share it for HR review to ensure tone and policy alignment before we finalise A3.

On the micro-break protocol for T4, I want to flag two points: 1) duration: most exercises should fit into 1 to 3 minutes so they can be slotted between calls or visitors; 2) visibility: some staff may feel awkward doing movements in front of customers, so we should prioritise subtle options for reception and slightly more visible ones for the contact centre back office. I will reflect this in A4 and mark which exercises are best for which setting.

Thanks for calling that out. Before we approve A4, I will need to run the exercises through our health and safety lens as part of T11, using A7 as a checklist. That includes checking for any issues with people who have mobility limitations or existing conditions. Please share a draft of A4 once you are ready so I can review it with our health and safety contact.

On T7, I will start assembling the training materials based on your module outline. Plan is: a short slide deck per module, plus a combined one-page job aid in A3 with key phrases, do and do not examples, and a simple de-escalation flow. I will keep the language plain and check with HR for any wording that might conflict with policy before we print or upload anything.

One concern from the floor is time pressure. Could we design each communication module so that the core content fits into about 45 minutes, with optional extras if time allows? That would make it easier to schedule around shifts later in T6. Maybe we prioritise the first two modules for everyone and offer the third as a slightly shorter, more reflective session.

We can structure it that way. For D3, my proposal is that we confirm the three modules as: 1) Handling angry or distressed customers; 2) Clear, calm language and boundaries; 3) Recovering and supporting colleagues. Modules 1 and 2 would be mandatory for all pilot participants, and module 3 would be a shorter session that we still include in the pilot but with more flexibility on timing. If that works, we can treat these as the final set for A3 and T3.

From HR, I am comfortable with those three modules and the split between core and shorter reflective content. They respond directly to the stressors we captured in A1 and will be easy to explain in the program overview A2. Please just make sure any examples avoid sensitive personal data and stay within our equality and dignity at work policies, which I will double-check under T11.

Understood. I will finalise a draft of A4 with 7 exercises: 3 seated, 2 standing, 1 breathing-focused, and 1 optional slightly more dynamic movement for those who want it. Each will include clear contraindications and alternatives. Once done, I will send it to you for the T11 review so we can adjust anything that might conflict with health and safety guidance.

To summarise where we are: we are converging on three communication modules for A3, with modules 1 and 2 as core and module 3 as a shorter reflective session. On wellbeing, we are aiming for 6 to 8 low-impact desk-based exercises in A4, with clear guidance on duration, visibility, and safety. If no one objects, I will note these as the final module set and wellbeing components in the program overview A2 so we can move on to scheduling and logistics.

I have now reviewed the draft of A4 against our checklist in A7. The exercises are low impact, include alternatives, and respect our guidance on inclusivity and safety. With that, I am comfortable saying that, subject to a brief sign-off from our health and safety contact, we can approve this wellbeing and micro-break protocol for the pilot.

Given HRs review and the alignment with frontline needs, I suggest we formally approve the current version of A4 as the desk-based wellbeing and micro-break protocol for the pilot, with any minor tweaks from health and safety treated as refinements rather than major changes. That will let us integrate it into the training plan and job aids under T7.

threads.thread_goal: Lock training schedule and logistics with minimal service impact.

messages.text: I have posted a draft training schedule in A5 for review. It covers the 18 pilot participants we confirmed in A2, with three communication modules and short wellbeing segments built in. For T6, I have tried to align sessions with shift patterns so that no team drops below minimum staffing. Please review the slots, especially for reception, and flag any conflicts before we treat this as final.

Looking at A5, the reception slots mostly work, but the late-shift session on Wednesday overlaps with a regular delivery window when we need two people at the desk. Could we move that group to an earlier slot on the same day or to Thursday morning? I want to avoid any risk of the desk being left with only one person during busy times.

Good catch. We can move that reception group to Thursday morning without affecting contact centre coverage. I will adjust A5 and T6 accordingly. For the contact centre pods, I have kept groups small and staggered so that each shift always has at least the minimum number of agents on the floor. If anyone spots a clash with planned campaigns or system work, please shout.

Once we agree on the final slots in A5, I will use them to complete T5: a one-page overview and invitation that clearly states dates, times, and expectations. That will go out via email and intranet, and we will ask supervisors to reinforce attendance. Please let me know if there are any blackout periods I should explicitly mention as off-limits in the comms.

From HR, the main blackout periods are payroll cut-off days and the monthly all-staff briefing. I do not see any clashes with those in A5, but please add a note in the T5 overview that sessions are mandatory unless there is an urgent operational issue, in which case rescheduling will be arranged with supervisors. That will help with expectations and with T8 attendance tracking later.

For reception, Thursday morning works better. One more detail: could we avoid scheduling both reception staff from the same shift in the same session? If one of them is delayed returning, we would be exposed. Maybe pair one early and one late shift person per session so there is always someone familiar with each pattern available.

Yes, I can reshuffle the reception names so each session mixes early and late shift staff. I will update A5 with that change and highlight the revised rows. This should still keep us within the staffing thresholds we agreed for T6. Once that is done, I think the schedule will be stable enough to approve, unless HR sees any remaining issues.

I will wait for your final update to A5 and then plug the confirmed dates and times into the T5 overview and invitations. I will also add a short note about how no-shows will be handled, but I would like us to agree on a simple process for that in this thread so we are consistent across teams.

On no-shows for T8, my suggestion is: trainers record attendance in A5 at the start of each session; any absent participant is flagged to their supervisor the same day; supervisors then agree a rescheduled slot within the pilot window, using any spare capacity in the schedule. If someone repeatedly misses sessions without a valid reason, we escalate to line management. Does that feel workable from an operations point of view?

That process sounds fine for reception. I would just add that if someone misses module 1, they should attend that before module 2 or 3, otherwise the content will not make as much sense. Maybe we can mark priority reschedule slots for module 1 in A5 so supervisors know where to place people who missed the first session.

Agree with the overall approach. For the contact centre, we can also use our existing coaching slots as backup times for rescheduled sessions, as long as we coordinate to avoid peak call periods. I will add a column in A5 to mark preferred reschedule options per group so T8 is easier to manage in practice.

To summarise the no-show process: trainers update attendance in A5; any absence is flagged to supervisors the same day; supervisors use marked reschedule slots or coaching times to rebook within the pilot window, prioritising module 1 if missed; repeated unexplained absences are escalated to line management. I will include this summary in the T5 overview so expectations are clear.

I have reviewed the latest version of A5 after your adjustments. From HR, I can confirm that the schedule respects minimum staffing levels, avoids our blackout periods, and gives all 18 pilot participants access to the three modules and wellbeing segments. I am comfortable approving this as the final training schedule for the pilot.

Great, thanks. I will lock A5 now and treat it as the reference for trainers and supervisors. Any minor tweaks from here will go through this channel so we keep a clear record. @605, you can now finalise T5 and share the invitations, and we will be ready to move into delivery under T8.

threads.thread_goal: Ensure compliance and define governance for ongoing rollout.

messages.text: Sharing initial policy review notes and a draft governance proposal. Using A7, I have checked the program elements against working time, breaks, equality, and dignity at work policies as part of T11. I have also started a draft of A8 to clarify who owns content, scheduling, and evaluation for future waves under T10 and T12. Please review and comment before we sign anything off.

Thanks for pulling this together. From an admin perspective, I suggest we formalise in A8 that HR owns the overall program design and compliance checks, while operations (contact centre and reception) own scheduling and day-to-day implementation. I can take the lead on documenting roles and responsibilities for T10, but I will need your input and sign-off, plus confirmation from the supervisors.

On the operations side, I am happy for the contact centre to own scheduling for our teams and to coordinate with HR on content updates. For T12, I also propose that supervisors run a short wellbeing check-in once per week using a simple script, and that we log any major themes so HR can see patterns over time. That could be part of the governance note in A8.

For reception, I can mirror that approach: I will own scheduling for our team and run the weekly check-ins using the same T12 script so we are consistent. One question on compliance: are there any limits on how often we can encourage micro-breaks during a shift, or is it enough that they fit within existing break rules and do not extend total working time?

Good question. Based on A7 and our working time policy, we can encourage short micro-breaks as long as they are brief, do not replace formal breaks, and do not extend the total shift length. The exercises in A4 are designed to be 1 to 3 minutes, which is acceptable. We just need to be clear in guidance that these are short pauses within working time, not additional rest breaks.

From a wellbeing perspective, that aligns with how I designed the exercises in A4. I will add a short note in the protocol clarifying that these micro-breaks are meant to be integrated into normal work flow and do not change formal break entitlements. That should help avoid misunderstandings and support your T11 documentation.

On T10, I propose the following structure for A8: 1) Content owner: HR, with input from supervisors and the fitness instructor; 2) Schedule owner: contact centre and reception supervisors; 3) Data and evaluation owner: HR, using A5 and A6; 4) Governance group: a small trio (HR, one supervisor, and myself) meeting quarterly to review feedback and decide updates. Does that cadence feel realistic?

Quarterly review sounds reasonable. I would also suggest a lighter touch after each pilot wave: a short debrief between HR and supervisors to capture immediate lessons before the formal quarterly review. That can feed into A6 and then into any updates to A3 or A4. We can note this as part of the review cadence in A8.

I am comfortable with HR owning content and evaluation, and with supervisors owning scheduling and local implementation. For T11, I have now completed the formal check against labour legislation and internal policies using A7. There are no blockers, just the clarifications we already discussed on micro-breaks and inclusive language. I will attach a short compliance note to the program overview and governance doc.

On T12, could we agree a simple check-in script that both contact centre and reception use? Something like: 1) How are you feeling energy-wise today; 2) Any difficult interactions this week; 3) Have you been able to use the micro-breaks or communication tools. That would keep it short but focused on the program themes.

I like that structure. We can add one more optional question: any suggestion to make the tools easier to use. I will draft this into a short script for T12 and share it with HR for a quick review, then we can include it as an appendix to A8 so it is easy to find.

To summarise the governance proposal for A8: HR owns content, compliance, and evaluation; contact centre and reception supervisors own scheduling and weekly check-ins under T12; an admin lead (me) supports documentation and coordination; and we hold quarterly reviews plus short post-wave debriefs. If everyone is aligned, I will finalise A8 with this structure and circulate for formal confirmation.

Given the completed checks in A7 and the absence of policy conflicts, I am comfortable stating that the program, as currently designed in A2, A3, and A4, complies with our labour legislation and internal HR policies. I will log this formally in T11 and attach the compliance note to the program overview and governance documents.

With compliance confirmed and governance roles clear, I suggest we treat the current version of A8 as our agreed model for ongoing rollout, subject to minor tweaks after the first pilot wave. That will give us a stable framework for scheduling, check-ins under T12, and future content updates.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot feedback and decide on adjustments before scaling.

messages.text: I have uploaded a draft Feedback & Impact Evaluation Report in A6 based on the survey and quick metrics from T9. Response rate was just over 70 percent, and we have pre and post data on stress and confidence, plus some qualitative comments. Please review the summary tables and themes so we can decide what to keep, change, or drop before the next wave.

Looking at A6, the main positives from contact centre staff are: clearer structure for difficult calls, appreciation for the role-plays, and the breathing exercise as a quick reset. The main issues are: some felt rushed in module 2, and a few said they struggled to remember all the phrases from the job aid in A3. For the next wave, I would suggest we simplify the language and build in a bit more practice time.

From the reception side, feedback in A6 shows that people liked the practical examples and the chance to share experiences, but some of the call-centre-focused scenarios felt less relevant. Also, a couple of colleagues mentioned that the standing stretches from A4 were hard to do when the lobby was busy. Maybe we can tailor one or two scenarios more to face-to-face situations and emphasise the more discreet exercises for reception.

On the wellbeing side, A6 shows that most participants tried at least two of the micro-break exercises, but regular use dropped after the first week. People said they forgot or felt self-conscious. For the next wave, I recommend we keep the current set in A4 but add a very short reminder routine that supervisors can use in their T12 check-ins, plus maybe a small visual cue at desks to normalise the exercises.

For the communication materials in A3, I can work on simplifying the phrasing and reducing the number of example sentences so the job aid is easier to remember. We could also highlight 3 or 4 key phrases per module as the main takeaways. That should address the feedback about overload without changing the core structure we agreed under D3.

On the metrics side, A6 shows an average drop of about one point on the stress scale and an increase of around one and a half points on confidence in handling difficult interactions. Escalation numbers for the pilot group also dipped slightly compared to the previous month, though the sample is small. This suggests the core approach is working, but we have room to improve relevance and habit-building.

Given that, my initial view on the next wave is: keep all three communication modules but adjust pacing and simplify the job aid; keep the wellbeing protocol but strengthen reminders and normalisation; and tweak scenarios so each team sees more of their own reality. I do not think we should drop any major element at this stage, but we should refine how we deliver it.

I agree. For reception, the main change I would like is more tailored scenarios and maybe slightly shorter group discussions so we can fit them around front-desk peaks. I would keep the breathing exercise and the most discreet stretches from A4, and perhaps present the others as optional extras rather than core content for everyone.

That makes sense. For the next wave, I suggest we mark two or three exercises in A4 as core for all teams and label the rest as optional. I can also create a very simple visual reminder, like a small desk card with the breathing pattern and one posture reset, to support habit-building without adding cost.

To capture this clearly for D9, I propose we document in A6 and A2 that we will: 1) keep all three communication modules but streamline content and emphasise a small set of key phrases; 2) keep the wellbeing protocol but define core versus optional exercises and add simple reminders; 3) adjust scenarios to be more team-specific and slightly shorten some discussions. Anything else you would add or remove from that list?

I would add one more adjustment: for T12, we should integrate one or two of the survey questions into the regular check-ins so we keep a light-touch pulse between waves. That will help us see if stress and confidence levels hold up over time without running full surveys too often.

Good point. We can add a quick rating question to the T12 script, like: on a scale from 1 to 5, how manageable have your interactions felt this week. We will not track names, just themes, and share aggregated impressions with HR for the next update of A6.

With those additions, I am comfortable saying we should keep the overall structure of the program, refine the content and pacing, and adjust how we support ongoing use of the tools. I do not see any element that clearly needs to be dropped at this stage, given the positive trends in A6.

Let me summarise the proposed decisions for D9: Keep all three communication modules and the wellbeing protocol; Change by simplifying the job aid in A3, marking core versus optional exercises in A4, tailoring scenarios by team, and adding reminders and light-touch check-in questions under T12; Drop nothing major, but we will shorten some discussions to fit better around operations. If everyone agrees, I will update A2 and A6 to reflect this and treat it as our plan for the next wave.

That summary matches my reading of A6 and the feedback from stakeholders. From HR, I support those adjustments as the basis for the next wave. I will also note in T9 that we may refine the survey slightly to focus on the most informative questions, now that we have seen what works.
